Attached: 1 image

#MAGA has failed to find evidence that trans people are more violent than cis people, so now the NIJ is offering big grants to any researchers (or "researchers") who can find a link between gender dysphoria and violent crime.  

If I thought I could get the grant (yeah no; I made the wrong professional choice for that a decade or more ago) and remain independent while doing it (seems unlikely) I would apply for that grant and word my proposal so very carefully. I think it wouldn't be difficult at all to find that a subset of men (i.e., men deep in the redpill / #incel universe) are at high risk of committing violence fueled by gender dysphoria: their concerns that they are not manly enough drive violence against women and other men. They wish they fit a specific kind of #masculinity more than they do. We see that over and over again in mass shootings.

Of course we're more familiar with a person feeling like their psychological sense of gender doesn't fit their physical realities when it's a trans or gender diverse person, but it makes sense that this should also apply to people whose idea of themselves is significantly more hegemonically mascuine than their life and their body would suggest. That is also logically #GenderDysphoria, right?

I made a handy graphic (investing for purposes of this argument in a problematic unidimensional gender binary) to help demonstrate my point. 

  * 1: Trans man
  * 2: Trans woman
  * 3: Cis woman feeling she belongs in a more feminine body
  * 4: Cis man feeling he belongs in a more masculine body

#masculinity #uspol #research
